styleHead: East Asian ink-wash illustration for a strategy game card, late Han dynasty China around 200 CE. Monochrome sumi ink on aged warm paper with a single restrained accent of antique bronze-gold. Dry-brush texture, strong silhouette, generous empty space in the upper third, dark vignette at the edges so it sits on a near-black interface. Vertical 2:3 composition, single clear subject, no border, no frame, no text, no letters, no calligraphy, no seals, no watermark, no modern objects.

cards.scene: Soldiers with spears crouching hidden among tall reeds and wooded hills beside a narrow mountain road, seen from behind them, an unsuspecting column of troops far below on the road.
A hillside ridge lined with many banners and straw dummies and campfire smoke to fake a large army, only a handful of real soldiers tending them.
A county granary and timber stockpile burning at night, flames rendered in the bronze-gold accent, a lone figure with a torch slipping away in the foreground.
A plain-clothed scout on a wooded hill overlooking a walled town and its army camp at dusk, counting tents, a bamboo slip tucked in his sash.
A rammed-earth fortress wall with its gate barred and defenders standing firm behind battlements, fields outside stripped bare, a besieging host small in the distance.
A calm strategist in scholar's robes seated at a low table with a field map, one hand raised, his gaze piercing through drifting smoke that reveals hidden enemy soldiers behind it.
